acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: Transferred on 11 January 2002 from the Office of the Lieutenant Governor, Richmond, VA.

bioghist.head: Biographical Information
bioghist.p: John Hager was born on August 28, 1936, in Durham, North Carolina, the second of two children of Ruth and Virgil Hager. He graduated from Durham High School in 1954, and from Purdue University in 1958 with a degree in Mechanical Engineering, before proceeding to Harvard, where he received an MBA in 1960. John Hager married Margaret Dickinson Chase in 1971.

John Hager served in the U.S. Army and in the Army Reserves, where he attained the rank of captain. He started working for the American Tobacco Company in 1961 and rose to the rank of Executive Vice President before being stricken with polio in 1973. After contracting polio, he lost the ability to use his legs and from then on utilized a wheelchair for mobility, but returned to work at American Tobacco and remained there until he retired in 1994. On January 17, 1998, Lt. Governor Hager was sworn in as Virginia thirty-fourth lieutenant governor, where he presided over the General Assembly and served as a member of several commissions. In 2001, he ran an unsuccessful campaign for nomination as the Republican candidate for Governor of Virginia.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: These records consist of Correspondence, Press Office files and Commission records, 1998-2002. The correspondence files include incoming and outgoing correspondence, as well as electronic mail received with corresponding responses. Press Office files are divided into photographs, press releases, speeches and a printout of the Lieutenant Governor's official website. The commission records document the Lieutenant Governor's involvement with several commissions including the Virginia State Crime Commission, Disability Commission, Commission of Educational Infrastructure and Technology, Faith-Based Community Services Task Force, and the Governor's Commission on Transportation Policy.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: This collection is arranged into three series:

list.item: Series II. Press Office files, 1998-2002; and

scopecontent.p: Series I: Correspondence, 1998-2001. This series documents the incoming and outgoing correspondence of the Office of the Lieutenant Governor. Correspondence is divided into three subseries: I. Incoming correspondence, 1998-2001; II. Outgoing correspondence, 1998-2001; III. Electronic mail correspondence, 1998-2001. The majority of the incoming and outgoing correspondence is to and from the Secretary of the Commonwealth and involves recommendations for appointments to various state positions and boards. The e-mail correspondence consists mainly of constituent mail and includes a copy of the incoming e-mail and a copy of the Lt. Governor's response.

Series II: Press Office files, 1998-2002. The Press Office files document the Lieutenant Governor's public relations activities, public appearances, official statements and his presence on the world wide web. This series includes the following subseries: I. Photographs, 1998-2001; II. Press releases, 1998-2002; III. Speeches, 1998-2001; and IV. Web site, 2001. The photographs document the Lt. Governor's attendance at various events and are undated. The official press releases of the Office of the Lieutenant Governor document John Hager's activities, initiatives, statements, appointments, legislative initiatives and stands on various issues. Starting in 1999 weekly schedules were released by the Press Office and can be found among the press releases. The typed speeches document the Lieutenant Governor's remarks at various speaking engagements throughout the Commonwealth, as well as documenting his activities, topical interests, and stands on various issues. The Web site subseries consists of a paper printout of the Lieutenant Governor's Web site that includes biographical information, information on policies and issues for 2001, listing of commissions and boards on which the Lt. Governor served, staff directory, list of press releases and speeches for 2001, and a family page.

Series III. Commission records, 1998-2002. The Lieutenant Governor served on several commissions that worked to formulate and recommend policy solutions for complex issues facing the Commonwealth. These records include meeting agendas and schedules, correspondence, supporting and background documentation, reports, legislative information, minutes, presentation materials, member lists, and related publications. Lieutenant Governor Hager served on the following commissions that are documented in this series: Commission on Family Violence Prevention, Virginia State Crime Commission, Disability Commission, Commission of Educational Infrastructure, Special Task Force Faith-Based Community Services, and the Governor's Commission on Transportation Policy.
